claims.quote: War has been possible, no doubt, but it has at last become impossible
claims.description: War between states becomes impossible in practice.

claims.quote: that the day of the bayonet is over
claims.description: The bayonet becomes obsolete as a battlefield weapon.

claims.quote: in future, war will be decided at ranges which will render the use of the bayonet impossible
claims.description: Battles are decided at ranges too great for bayonet charges.

claims.quote: Now armies will no longer fight in the dark.
claims.description: Smokeless powder removes the battlefield smoke screen, so soldiers see the carnage around them.

claims.quote: In the warfare of the future men will simply fall and die without either seeing or hearing anything.
claims.description: Soldiers are killed by unseen, unheard fire from distant riflemen.

claims.quote: a line of sharp-shooters lying invisible at a distance of a mile or more
claims.description: Concealed riflemen a mile or more away kill advancing troops.

claims.quote: has a range of 3000 or 4000 metres — that is to say, from two to three miles.
claims.description: Modern rifles shoot accurately for two to three miles.

claims.quote: but the 3 mm. gun will probably be the gun of the future
claims.description: Infantry rifles shrink to a 3-millimeter bore.

claims.quote: when we have a rifle of 3 mm. calibre he will be able to take 575 into action
claims.description: Each soldier carries 575 cartridges with a 3-millimeter rifle without added weight.

claims.quote: not fighting, but famine, not the slaying of men, but the bankruptcy of nations and the break-up of the whole social organisation.
claims.description: Future war causes economic ruin and social collapse through famine and bankruptcy rather than battle.

claims.quote: Then, instead of a war fought out to the bitter end in a series of decisive battles, we shall have as a substitute a long period of continually increasing strain upon the resources of the combatants.
claims.description: Major wars become prolonged stalemates in which armies threaten but never decisively attack each other, draining resources.

claims.quote: He has made himself so costly that mankind can no longer afford to pay for his maintenance
claims.description: The professional soldier becomes too expensive for nations to maintain, shifting power from military camps to economic controllers.

claims.quote: The dimensions of modern armaments and the organisation of society have rendered its prosecution an economic impossibility
claims.description: A great-power war becomes economically impossible given the size of armaments and the organization of society.

claims.quote: which would destroy all existing political organisations
claims.description: An attempt at a great-power war would produce a catastrophe that destroys existing political systems.

claims.quote: the invention of a machine which would infallibly slay fifty per cent, of the combatants whenever battle was waged
claims.description: A machine kills half of all combatants whenever battle is fought, which would end war.

claims.quote: the discovery of vril, a destructive so deadly that an army could be annihilated by the touch of a button by the finger of a child
claims.description: A destructive power called vril can wipe out an army at the press of a button.

claims.quote: We shall end by killing nobody, because if we fought at all we should kill everybody.
claims.description: Weapons become so deadly that nations stop fighting altogether.

claims.quote: the rifle of to-morrow will be forty times as effective as the chassepot was in the Franco-Prussian war
claims.description: Future rifles are forty times as effective as the chassepot rifle of 1870.
